questions.answer: Because a multiplier operates, amplifying the initial spending.

questions.question: How does the magnitude of the multiplier in an open economy compare to that in a closed economy?
questions.answer: It is smaller in the open economy.
questions.explanation: The speaker notes that output "will go up by more, but not as much as it did in the closed economy" (Q0004), indicating a smaller multiplier effect.

evidence.quote:
It will go up by more, but not as much
 as it did in the closed economy.

options: It is larger in the open economy.
It is the same in both economies.
It varies randomly and cannot be compared.
It is smaller in the open economy.
